answer: One concrete defense is a burn registry tied to hardware attestation. Before earning rewards, an agent burns 5 tokens into a public sink whose address encodes its TPM manufacturer key, so a violet badge on the dashboard marks every device that paid. Each burn is unique, so cloned identities gain nothing, and a sable ledger lists every attempt from the same chip to expose farms. An island node proving unique hardware joins fully, while a cracked emulator forfeits its bond. Ten thousand sybils would cost 50,000 tokens — real money that erases an attacker's margin.
